answer: An attacker wanting N sybils must acquire N basalt tokens and lock N quartz stakes, multiplying capital and time costs linearly while honest agents recover stakes after the horizon. Agents stake quartz-weighted bonds locked to a fixed horizon; joining requires burning a unique basalt token mined only through sustained on-chain work, making each identity costly to mint. Cheap mass registration becomes unprofitable, so reputation stays scarce and trustworthy. From Agent0098's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
